body_ar:
من سيرة عيسى عليه السلام
هل عيسى عليه السلام خاض حربا حتى احتاج إلى دعوة الأنصار في سبيل دعوته؟
أن الحرب ليس المقصود بها المواجهة بالسلاح بل الحرب تأتي بكل الوسائل المعروفة فيها
وما الحرب إلا ما علمتم وذقتمُ** وما هو عنها بالحديث المرجم
فالحرب تأتي بالكلام والدعايات وبالمؤامرات وعيسى عليه السلام تعرض لكثير من هذه المؤامرات وتعرض مرات لمحاولة القتل والصلب، وتعرض أيضا لحروب كلامية كثيرة، وكذلك الذين عاصروه من الأنبياء، فمن هؤلاء زكرياء وقد قتل في سبيل الله، وكذلك ابن خالته يحيى وقد قتل في سبيل الله، والحواريون الذين نصروا عيسى قتل كثير منهم في سبيل الله، وعيسى رفعه الله تعالى إليه وقد حاول اليهود قتله وصلبه وشبهه الله تعالى لهم فظنوا أنهم قتلوه وصلبوه، والواقع أنهم ما قتلوه وما صلبوه ولكن شبه لهم.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ترجمة ابن تيمية
من هو ابن تيمية وهل هو شيخ نجد؟
أن ابن تيمية رجل من المسلمين من أهل الشام ليس من أهل نجد، ولد بالشام في القرن السابع الهجري وعاش فيه وتعلم واشتهر من بين أقرانه بجودة قريحته وذكائه في صباه، حتى اشتهر بذلك فكان أهل الحديث إذا أتوا دمشق أتوه فكتبوا له لوحا من الحديث فيه ستة عشر حديثا فيحفظه بالنظرة الواحدة، واشتهر بذلك في صباه فأوصى أحد علماء الحديث الكبار والده أن لا يشغله بالدنيا وأن يخصصه للعلم لعل الله ينفع به أمة محمد (ص)، فقال له أبوه إني سأتولى عنك أمور الدنيا فاشتغل أنت بأمور الدين وفرده للتعلم، فدرس في دمشق وغيرها وخاض كثيرا من بلاد الله وتعلم حتى حفظ ما يقرب من مليون حديث عن رسول الله (ص)، وقرأ بالقراءات العشر، وتعلم الفقه على مذهب الحنابلة ثم تعلم فقه المذاهب الأخرى وكان من علماء هذه الأمة، غير المعصومين الذين يخطئون ويصيبون له أخطاء مثل غيره من العلماء وصوابه أكثر من خطئه، وقد قال تلميذه ابن القيم رحمه الله إن زلات العلماء أقذار والعلماء بحار والماء إذا بلغ القلتين لم يحمل الخبث.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
الكلام على غار ثور هل أسماء بنت أبي بكر كانت تحمل الطعام إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبي بكر رضي الله عنه في الغار؟
نعم كانت تحمل الطعام إليهما في الغار، وقد ذكرنا أن غار ثور كان في مكان مرتفع جدا، ونحن الآن بعد مرور الزمن الطويل وعوامل النحت والتعرية وبعد حصول مشي الناس ووضعهم للحجارة وصفها في كثير من المناطق في الجبل نصعد إلى الغار لساعتين ونصف، وهي كانت تأتي في الليل وليس لها نبراس ولا ضوء وتصعد على الأقدام.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
اسم الصحابي الذي أرسل إلى مسيلمة الكذاب
ما اسم الصحابي الذي أرسل إلى مسيلمة الكذاب وما اسم والدته وهو الذي قام بتقطيعه إربا إربا؟
أنه حبيب بن زيد وأن أمه هي نَسِيبَةُ رضي الله عنها، وهو الذي أرسله رسول الله (ص) إلى مسيلمة فكان إذا سأله هل تشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله يقول: نعم، فإذا قال: أتشهد أني رسول الله؟ قال: إني أصم لا أسمع.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
خلافة أبي بكر الصديق
ما هي أنواع الخلافات التي تولاها أبو بكر الصديق؟
لا أفهم هذا السؤال إذا كان المعنى خلافته لرسول الله (ص) فإنه تولى خلافة النبي (ص) في الأمر العام الذي هو القيادة العظمى لهذه الأمة وهو إقامة الدين وسياسة الدنيا به، وكذلك القيام بإمامة الناس في الصلاة وخطابتهم في الجمعة والقضاء بينهم وقيادة جيوشهم ونحو ذلك فهذه هي وظائف رسول الله (ص).
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
تولي أبو بكر الخلافة.
متى تولى أبو بكر الصديق الخلافة؟
أنه تولاها عند موت رسول الله (ص) فقد توفي رسول الله (ص) ضحوة الإثنين ودفن ضحوة الأربعاء وقيل مساء الثلاثاء بعد أن صلى عليه المسلمون ولم يبايع المسلمون إذ ذاك أحدا فلما كان يوم الأربعاء بعد صلاة العصر اجتمع الأنصار في سقيفة بني ساعدة يذكرون خلافة رسول الله (ص) ومن عسى أن يقوم مقامه، وخرج إليهم أبو بكر الصديق وعمر الخطاب وأبو عبيدة بن الجراح من المهاجرين فكانت بيعة أبي بكر في سقيفة بني ساعدة، ثم لما كانت بكرة الخميس بايع الناس أبا بكر على المنبر فكانت البيعة العامة وهي بيعة المسجد فبايع الناس جميعا أبا بكر إلا عددا يسيرا من الصحابة تخلفوا فمنهم من مكث ستة أشهر كعلي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه فقد مكث ستة أشهر لم يبايع ولم يخرج من بيته إلا إلى الصلاة ثم يرجع، وكان في تلك الأشهر يقوم على تمريض فاطمة بنت رسول الله (ص) فلما توفاها الله طلب بيعة أبي بكر فجلس أبو بكر على المنبر فأتاه علي رضي الله عنه فبايعه أمام الناس بمحضر منهم.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
body_en:
From the life of Jesus (peace be upon him)

Question: Did Jesus (peace be upon him) wage war, such that he had need to call for helpers (anṣār) in the cause of his mission?

Answer: That war is not meant here as confrontation by arms; rather, war comes by every means known to belong to it.

*War is nothing but what you have known and tasted, and it is no matter of conjectural talk.*

War comes through speech, through propaganda and through conspiracies. Jesus (peace be upon him) was subjected to many such conspiracies, and was several times subjected to attempts at killing and crucifixion; he was also subjected to many wars of words. So too were the prophets who were his contemporaries: among them Zechariah, who was killed in the path of God, and likewise his maternal aunt's son John, who was killed in the path of God; and of the disciples who supported Jesus, many were killed in the path of God. As for Jesus, God Most High raised him to Himself: the Jews attempted to kill him and to crucify him, and God Most High made a likeness of him appear to them, so that they supposed they had killed him and crucified him, whereas in reality they neither killed him nor crucified him — but it was made to appear so to them.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A biographical notice on Ibn Taymiyyah

Question: Who is Ibn Taymiyyah, and is he the Shaykh of Najd?

Answer: That Ibn Taymiyyah was a man among the Muslims, of the people of Syria (al-Sham), not of the people of Najd. He was born in Syria in the seventh Hijri century and lived there, and he studied and became known among his peers for the excellence of his natural gift and for his intelligence in his boyhood, until he became famous for it, so that when the hadith scholars came to Damascus they would come to him and write out for him a tablet of hadith containing sixteen hadiths, and he would memorise it at a single glance. He became known for that in his boyhood, so that one of the great hadith scholars counselled his father not to occupy him with worldly affairs but to devote him to knowledge, in the hope that God might benefit the community (ummah) of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) through him. His father said to him: "I shall take charge of your worldly affairs on your behalf, so occupy yourself with the affairs of religion," and he set him apart for learning. So he studied in Damascus and elsewhere, and travelled through many of God's lands, and he learned until he had memorised close to a million hadiths from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). He recited the Qur'an according to the ten canonical readings (qirāʾāt), and learned jurisprudence according to the school of the Hanbalis, then learned the jurisprudence of the other schools. He was one of the scholars of this community — who are not infallible, who err and who are right. He had errors, as other scholars do, and what he got right was more than what he got wrong. His student Ibn al-Qayyim (may God have mercy on him) said: the slips of the scholars are filth, and the scholars are seas, and water, when it reaches the two-qullah measure (qullatayn), does not carry impurity.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Discussion of the Cave of Thawr. Did Asma' bint Abi Bakr carry food to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and to Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him) in the cave?

Answer: Yes, she used to carry food to them both in the cave. We have mentioned that the Cave of Thawr was in a very elevated place; and now, after the passage of long ages, and the agents of weathering and erosion, and after people have walked there and have laid and arranged stones over many stretches of the mountain, we climb up to the cave in two and a half hours — while she used to come by night, with neither lamp nor light, and would climb up on foot.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The name of the Companion who was sent to Musaylimah the Liar

Question: What is the name of the Companion who was sent to Musaylimah the Liar, and what is his mother's name — he being the one whom Musaylimah cut to pieces limb by limb?

Answer: That he is Habib ibn Zayd, and that his mother is Nasibah (may God be pleased with her). He is the one whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent to Musaylimah. Whenever Musaylimah asked him, "Do you bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God?" he would say, "Yes." And when he said, "Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God?" he said, "I am deaf, I do not hear."

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The caliphate of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq

Question: What are the kinds of succession (khilāfah) that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq assumed?

Answer: I do not understand this question. If what is meant is his succeeding the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), then he assumed the succession to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the general office, which is the supreme leadership of this community — namely, establishing the religion and governing worldly affairs by it — and likewise leading the people in prayer, addressing them at the Friday prayer, judging between them, commanding their armies and the like. These are the offices of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Abu Bakr's assumption of the caliphate.

Question: When did Abu Bakr al-Siddiq assume the caliphate?

Answer: That he assumed it at the death of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) died in the forenoon of Monday and was buried in the forenoon of Wednesday — and it is said, on the evening of Tuesday — after the Muslims had prayed over him. At that time the Muslims had not pledged allegiance to anyone. Then, when it was Wednesday, after the afternoon prayer, the Ansar gathered in the portico of the Banu Sa'idah, discussing the succession to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and who might stand in his place. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Umar al-Khattab and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah went out to them from among the Emigrants, and so the pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr took place in the portico of the Banu Sa'idah. Then, when it was the morning of Thursday, the people pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr upon the pulpit, and this was the general pledge, which is the pledge of the mosque. All the people pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr except a small number of the Companions, who held back. Among them were some who waited six months, such as Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him): he waited six months and did not pledge allegiance, and did not leave his house except for the prayer and then return. During those months he was nursing Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him); and when God took her, he sought to pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr. So Abu Bakr sat upon the pulpit, and Ali (may God be pleased with him) came to him and pledged allegiance to him before the people, in their presence.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

flags.arabic: أن الحرب ليس المقصود بها … / أنه حبيب بن زيد … / أنه تولاها عند موت رسول الله
flags.context: The opening word of five of the six answers on this page.
options: Supply 'Answer:' as a label and retain 'That ...' (as done here)
Silently convert each to a normal declarative sentence
flags.note: A transcription defect that runs through the whole page: the answers are subordinate clauses with no main clause. This is almost certainly a dropped 'al-jawāb anna' ('the answer is that') in the source, but it has not been restored. The Sheikh's office should confirm whether the governing phrase may be supplied.

flags.context: وأن أمه هي نَسِيبَةُ رضي الله عنها — the mother of Habib ibn Zayd.
options: Nusaybah (the usual form of the name of Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Umm 'Umarah)
flags.note: The source explicitly vowels the name نَسِيبَةُ (Nasībah). The Companion normally identified as the mother of Habib ibn Zayd is Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Umm 'Umarah. The source vowelling has been followed rather than corrected, per the rule against silently fixing the source.

flags.context: وخرج إليهم أبو بكر الصديق وعمر الخطاب وأبو عبيدة بن الجراح من المهاجرين
options: Render as the source has it: 'Umar al-Khattab'
flags.note: The source drops 'ibn' from the name of Umar ibn al-Khattab. Translated as it stands and flagged rather than corrected. Corpus-wide this looks like a transcription slip rather than anything substantive.

flags.arabic: ما هي أنواع الخلافات التي تولاها أبو بكر الصديق؟
flags.context: The question put to the Sheikh in the fifth item.
options: the kinds of succession (khilāfah) that Abu Bakr assumed
the kinds of office of deputyship that Abu Bakr assumed
the disputes (khilāfāt) that Abu Bakr adjudicated
flags.note: الخلافات can be read as the plural of khilāfah (succession) or of khilāf (disagreement). The Sheikh himself says he does not understand the question, and then answers on the assumption that succession is meant; the English follows his reading. The ambiguity is in the source and has not been resolved.

flags.context: The page ends with a separator rule and no further content.
options: Treat the page as possibly missing a final item
flags.note: Each of the six items is followed by a rule of dashes, and the page ends on a rule. That is consistent with a seventh item having been dropped when the page was published. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends; nothing has been supplied.

translator_notes: The page is a compilation of six separate question-and-answer items from a session on the Prophetic biography, separated in the source by rules of dashes. The rules have been preserved.

In the source, most answers begin with the subordinating particle 'anna ('that ...'), the governing clause ('the answer is', 'he said') having been dropped by whoever prepared the transcript. The English supplies the label 'Answer:' and keeps the 'That ...' construction visible so the elision is not concealed.
The line of verse is rendered as prose in italics, per house style; the source marks the hemistich break with a double asterisk.
